summary: Intl.NumberFormat formats numbers according to a chosen locale and options, including currency conventions.
documentation: Intl.NumberFormat formats numbers according to a chosen locale and options, including currency conventions. The formatter produces display text; it does not change the underlying stored amount or perform accounting calculations.
inputs: A locale, formatting options and a numeric value.
caution: Specify the locale and currency explicitly for deterministic examples. Do arithmetic in suitable numeric units before formatting.
scenarios: Display an invoice total using a consistent currency style.
Show a localized price in a checkout preview.
Format dashboard amounts without manually inserting separators.
title: Display cents as US dollars
problem: Input is an integer number of cents from -100000000 through 100000000. Return an en-US USD currency string using exactly two fractional digits and standard grouping. Examples: 123450 becomes $1,234.50; -500 becomes -$5.00.
goal: Use Intl.NumberFormat or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Divide cents by 100, then format with locale en-US, style currency and currency USD.
